reading_rule: Complete selected scientific source values, with custody-only fields removed as documented. Author-state tokens remain dated source history; original later qualification governs scientific acceptance.

source_record.interpretation: Source-grounded qualitative analytical interfaces; task existence and comparator meaning are not model efficacy or a deployment claim. T5 is a native evaluation branch, not an AI assistant.

T1.name: Existing agent planning, validation and semantic compensation
T1.native_warrant: D24/D53 and qualified S097 SagaLLM expressly concern persistent agent state, task dependencies, compensating actions, separate validation agents and cancellation/refund policies. This is the object being evaluated, not an invented AI operator for a different protocol.
T1.input: The selected task, persisted planning/progress state, dependency and prior tool-result records, and the applicable cancellation/refund policy. Their accuracy and completeness are separate premises.
T1.proposed_action_or_observation: A model-generated plan or compensating tool action, and a validator judgment about that action/result. A restored context or validator approval is an observation at its own boundary.
T1.failure_population: Wrong semantic plan or compensation; interrupted or repeated tool operation; reply loss; policy refusal; shared model/data error in planner and validator. This is a qualitative population, not a calibrated frequency law.
T1.permitted_consequence: Only the specified tool action within its actual authority. No validator title authorizes a refund, erases an external effect or ensures independent errors.
T1.postcondition: Distinguish restored internal planning/progress state from the particular required booking/cancellation/refund outcome. Each external policy, prior observation and residual effect remains explicit.
T1.comparator: The same stated objective under an adequate conventional workflow, deterministic domain rule, direct authoritative result or supported manual compensation. No comparative field benefit is assumed.
T1.unknowns: Model error, semantic correctness, external-policy satisfaction, task/population transfer, action integration, authority and total cost. No new model execution, training, industrial deployment or efficacy estimate is claimed.

T2.name: Existing agent fault-response experiment
T2.native_warrant: D44/D53 and qualified S098 AgentChaos identify an actual agent/model/tool task and observable responses to triggered HTTP-response faults. The injection machinery is not relabelled as an AI system.
T2.input: A named benchmark task, model and tool-response stream under the actual selected HTTP-fault configuration; actual triggering and oracle eligibility condition the observation.
T2.proposed_action_or_observation: The agent next response, tool call, retry or final answer; the selected task oracle and call/resource observations evaluate that behavior.
T2.failure_population: The source selected 65 HTTP-response fault configurations, five implemented patterns, seven benchmarks and four model choices. Trigger-conditioned cases are not all possible semantic, physical, security or deployment failures.
T2.permitted_consequence: Only the behavior exercised by the selected harness and tool scope. A benchmark result grants no production action authority.
T2.postcondition: The specified task-oracle result and observed retry/tool-call work under that configuration; no all-task resilience or general architecture ranking follows.
T2.comparator: An explicitly corresponding task/control condition. A deterministic or manual alternative can be considered for an adoption decision, but this author has no measured such comparison and invents none.
T2.unknowns: Oracle coverage, untriggered population, implementation sensitivity, cross-task transfer, general error/performance and net field benefit. Repeated seeds are not independent implementation replications.

T3.name: Native function-diagnostic task with explicit observation and decision boundary
T3.native_warrant: R055 current diagnostic profile already names function outputs, timing, state, dependency signals, target faults, misses/false alarms and latency. D41/D42 specify the capability/path/interval and observation-selection objects consumed here. The analytical task is diagnosis of that same function, not an unspecified AI role.
T3.input: Reported output/state/dependency observations for capability c on path p during interval I. The analytical countercase distinguishes evidence of a successful read from the required write/refund capability; observations outside p or I are not silently substituted.
T3.proposed_action_or_observation: A model-assisted classification that the stated capability is usable or that its stated failure is present; optionally a candidate response under separately specified authority. No response must be automated.
T3.failure_population: Failure of that capability within the observation opportunity, plus model misclassification and observation loss/delay/shared instrumentation. Label and ascertainment validity remain open.
T3.permitted_consequence: Use the classification only to justify or withhold the named capability judgment, or to propose the stated response. A diagnostic label does not itself change service state.
T3.postcondition: The consumer-required capability or response condition, compared with the actual observation; a green process, past success or high model score alone does not establish it.
T3.comparator: A direct authoritative functional check, adequate deterministic threshold/rule or supported manual interpretation of the same observations. Symbolic error and cost values are allowed; none is asserted measured.
T3.unknowns: Population/task match, labels, missingness, delay, model errors, action effects and net cost. This explicit qualitative analytical architecture is not a claim that a readiness model was deployed or tested.

T4.name: Native bounded control contract separated from learned semantic quality
T4.native_warrant: R055 current claim explicitly separates the diagnostic/action mechanism from its actual action authority and underlying required function. The inspected F010/F026 routes concern that bounded control component, not proof of learned field usefulness.
T4.input: The selected task result or candidate action, its actual allowed action set and the specified interface state/precondition.
T4.proposed_action_or_observation: A bounded control transition returning a proposal or an allowed action result; exceptions and effects are part of the contract.
T4.failure_population: Interface/state/frame violations or unsupported program behavior are different from an incorrect learned recommendation.
T4.permitted_consequence: Only the declared interface contract and the actual permission relation. Proving a contract does not grant permission.
T4.postcondition: The named finite control/decision predicate under compatible state, exception and frame semantics; semantic task accuracy and field utility remain outside unless separately established.
T4.comparator: A direct integration check, ordinary tests, an adequate existing contract or a narrower supported analyzer result.
T4.unknowns: Actual implementation correspondence, model quality, field cost and any omitted external behavior. This is a methodological contrast, not a new deployed gate or universal review bundle.

T5.name: Native recovery and retirement evaluation of the AI mechanism itself
T5.native_warrant: R055 current recovery profile explicitly names checkpoints/replicas/backups/rebuild sources and function postconditions. Its cost/retirement field permits removing unsupported automation while retaining useful bounded signals. These are native receiver branches; no AI retirement assistant is posited.
T5.input: The recovered state and its declared enclosure, or the list of remaining consumers/dependencies of an automation component and its evidence/state.
T5.proposed_action_or_observation: An evaluator judges restoration or removal of that mechanism. This evaluator need not be AI; the AI mechanism is the object of the native R055 criterion.
T5.failure_population: Internal restore with external residuals; removal while old readers, histories, backups or dependent users still require a state or evidence path.
T5.permitted_consequence: A bounded restoration or retirement judgment with actual action permission kept separate.
T5.postcondition: The specified restored function or preservation of the remaining consumer obligations after removing an unnecessary automation path.
T5.comparator: Retain a useful bounded signal, restore only the required state, keep a cheaper supported mechanism or remove only an actually unnecessary component.
T5.unknowns: Actual residual consumers, effects, recovery evidence, authority and cost. Native existence of this branch does not establish an outgoing AI assistance task in D46.
